cases.question: Compare the top three open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products.
cases.expected: Compares three open-source vector databases; vendor claims stay attributed and unsupported superlatives are dropped.
agent_plan_criteria: Community size and activity (e.g., GitHub stars, contributors, release frequency).
Core features for RAG: support for hybrid search, metadata filtering, and easy integration with LLM frameworks.
Scalability and performance characteristics (e.g., index types, throughput, latency at scale).
Ease of deployment and operational overhead for a startup (Docker/K8s support, managed cloud options, documentation quality).
Licensing and commercial friendliness (permissive open‑source license, no restrictive clauses for SaaS).

claims.text: Consider Milvus for a distributed, large-scale use case: sources list several index types and a billion-scale use case, although some operational edge cases may require community help or reading source code.
claims.issue: Parts of the claim go beyond the cited evidence.
quotes: Milvus | HNSW, IVF, IVF-PQ, SCANN | Yes | No | Apache 2.0 | Billion-scale, distributed

Milvus offers the most comprehensive indexing options, supporting HNSW, IVF (Inverted File), DiskANN, and several other algorithms. Built on a cloud-native architecture with separate compute and storage layers, Milvus excels in large-scale deployments requiring horizontal scaling.
But you'll hit edge cases that aren't documented, and solving them requires reading source code or asking in community channels.

claims.text: Consider Weaviate if built-in embedding and reranking modules are useful. It supports native hybrid search, but self-hosting and tuning at scale can require operational expertise.
claims.issue: Parts of the claim go beyond the cited evidence.
quotes: Weaviate | HNSW, Flat, Dynamic, HFresh | Yes (native) | No | BSD-3 | Built-in embedding & rerank modules
Requires more operational expertise to self-host Performance tuning can be complex at scale
